``
Set up a classic 2D dam-break case using the interFoam solver.
Set `application interFoam;` in `system/controlDict`.
Create a plain rectangular domain 0.584 m wide by 0.584 m tall using `blockMesh`.
Mesh the domain with 46 cells in x, 76 cells in y, and 1 cell in z with uniform grading `simpleGrading (1 1 1)`.
Assign patch type `empty` to the `frontAndBack` patches so the case is two-dimensional.
Use the Martin & Moyce (1952) benchmark geometry: a water column 0.1462 m wide by 0.2921 m tall sitting in the bottom-left corner of the tank.
Initialize the column with `setFields` so that `alpha.water = 1` inside the column box and `0` elsewhere in the domain.
Set gravity to (0 0 -9.81) m²/s in `constant/g`.
Use water properties rho 1000 kg/m³ and nu 1e-06 m²/s, and air properties rho 1 kg/m³ and nu 1.48e-05 m²/s, in `constant/physicalProperties` (or `transportProperties` depending on the OpenFOAM version).
Make the left, right, and bottom patches no-slip walls with fixed value velocity (0 0 0) and `zeroGradient` pressure (`p_rgh`).
Make the top patch an open atmosphere with `totalPressure` boundary condition (p0 = 0) for `p_rgh`, `pressureInletOutletVelocity` for U, and `zeroGradient` for `alpha.water` with a constant contact angle (`alphaContactAngle`) sub-entry.
Run laminar: set `simulationType laminar;` in `constant/momentumTransport` (or `constant/turbulenceProperties` depending on version).
Run the case for an end time of 1 s with adjustable time stepping, following the standard OpenFOAM `damBreak` tutorial settings (e.g., `adjustTimeStep yes; maxCo 1; maxDeltaT 1;`) with write intervals appropriate for post-processing the free-surface evolution.
